phase: M6 Phase 5D - Conversation Faithfulness & Context Integrity
net_code_change: ZERO - app/services/llm_generator.py was edited during investigation and reverted byte-for-byte to its pre-Phase-5D committed state (git diff empty)
executive_summary: Phase 5D was scoped around the hypothesis that ML-07/OOS-01 were caused by conversation-history fabrication. Live forensic reproduction using real, unmodified production code disproved this: the Conversation History section of the actual LLM prompt was correctly empty and labeled '(no prior conversation)' in both cases. The real, confirmed root cause is a generation-stage groundedness failure: HybridRetriever returns topically-irrelevant chunks that pass the 0.3 score threshold via generic semantic similarity, and the configured model (llama3, forced CPU-only) narrates that irrelevant content back to the user as though restating their question. Three single-call prompt-instruction fixes and one two-call relevance-gate architecture were attempted and live-tested; all were reverted after live testing showed each was either ineffective (OOS-01 never resolved in any attempt) or introduced a new, worse regression (attempt 3 caused a false decline on a perfectly-matched, 1.000-scoring, genuinely in-scope DBMS query). The phase ends with the root cause fully documented and evidenced, and zero net code shipped.

remaining_limitations: ML-07 and OOS-01 both remain CONFIRMED NOT FIXED - root cause understood and evidenced, no safe fix found within this phase's budget and constraints

The underlying defect is broader than the two named test cases - any out-of-scope query whose corpus doesn't cover the topic but still returns an above-threshold chunk via generic semantic similarity is a plausible trigger, not confined to the Machine Learning workspace or these two exact queries

Prompt-instruction tuning alone with the currently configured model (llama3, forced CPU-only) is not a reliable lever for this defect - evidence-backed conclusion from three failed attempts, one of which caused a new regression

A two-call relevance-gate architecture is plausible but substantially bigger than prompt tuning: requires LLM client protocol extension for JSON-mode, rewriting ~10+ existing unit tests encoding a one-call invariant, and a permanent 2x latency cost; semantic accuracy still unproven
Sections on document-history-spoofing, prompt-injection-style history claims, and ambiguous fresh messages were not independently live-probed this phase
No new regression tests were added since no fix was shipped to test
product_completeness_disclaimer: This product is NOT being described as fixed, complete, or free of this defect for the classes of query tested. It is not 'perfect' or '100% correct'. ML-07, OOS-01, and the broader class of out-of-scope-but-above-threshold queries in the Machine Learning workspace (and plausibly elsewhere) remain unresolved at the end of this phase.
recommended_next_phase: 1. A properly engineered two-call relevance gate using Ollama's format=json grammar-constrained decoding (not free-text parsing), with the existing unit-test invariant deliberately renegotiated and the 2x-latency cost measured and accepted or optimized (e.g. a smaller/faster classification-only model)

2. Re-evaluate whether llama3 is an adequate generation model for this product at all - this phase's live evidence suggests a genuine capability ceiling for instruction-following that prompt engineering cannot fully work around

3. Only after (1) or (2), revisit the retrieval-side score threshold / reranker lever this phase was explicitly forbidden from touching - the two problems (irrelevant chunks passing threshold, and the model narrating whatever it receives) are compounding, not independent
4. Complete the untested Phase 5D-6/5D-7/5D-8 probes (document-history-spoofing, prompt-injection-style history claims, ambiguous fresh messages) as a cheap, low-risk verification pass
